Jules Aurel Noukeu Jugnia, 17 ans, est m: Jules Aurel Noukeu Jugnia, 17, died of a heart attack during a basketball game. His friends and family pay tribute to him.
Chez Jules, un coin du logement est dédi: At Jules’s home, a corner of the apartment is dedicated to his memory. He lost his life at 17 while playing basketball.
Le 14 août, Beverley Jacques, directeur: On August 14, Beverley Jacques, director of the organization DOD Basketball, reached out to tell us that one of his basketball coaches had lost his life during a basketball game in Saint-Léonard.
Jules était un jeune de 17 ans très enga: Jules was a 17-year-old deeply involved in his neighbourhood, and for his entire community, it is imperative that his name not be forgotten. With that in mind, several members of DOD Basketball will ask the City of Montréal to rename the park where he lost his life after him.
J’ai rencontré plusieurs personnes qui o: I met several people who knew Jules, including colleagues, friends and community workers, and I went to his home to speak with his mother, his aunt and his grandmother.
Ce qui a été éprouvant, c’est de faire f: What was difficult was facing people devastated by Jules’s death. I offer my most sincere condolences to all his loved ones and truly hope I have paid a fitting tribute to this young man.
J’ai tenté de mettre de l’avant ce qu’ét: I tried to highlight who Jules was: a committed, loving young man who took care of his people and who aspired to a better future, for himself, but also and above all for others. At the basketball court where Jules died, many said they wanted to rename the place and give it his name. As a service to the community, I looked into the steps required to rename a court in Montréal. I hope this article will help Jules’s loved ones move forward with this project, and keep his name alive a little longer in his neighbourhood.
Je vous laisse découvrir l’impact qu’a e: I invite you to discover the impact of young Jules Aurel Noukeu Jugnia who, at 17, managed to move mountains through the strength of his commitment to his community.
Engagé, passionné, ambitieux – voilà les: Committed, passionate, ambitious – those are the words that best describe young Jules Aurel Noukeu Jugnia, who tragically lost his life during a basketball game on August 8. Jules died of a heart attack at 17.
Jules vibrait d’une joie de vivre énorme: Jules radiated an enormous joie de vivre. Jules was a son, a friend, a colleague, a young man. Today, hoping to ease the immense suffering of his mother and loved ones, friends are organizing a <l1>fundraiser</l1> to help cover the costs of the funeral and of repatriating Jules to Cameroon, his country of origin, where he will be laid to rest near his family.
« Tu nous as quittés en faisant ce que t: “You left us doing what you loved: playing sports in front of your friends, your work team and in the neighbourhood you spent your time in,” the organization DOD Basketball wrote in an Instagram post. Jules had been attending this community organization since he was 14 and had even become an employee and youth worker there. We met with members of his circle, whose goal is to keep his presence alive, despite his tragic end.
<strong>Paroles d’une mère endeuillée :: A grieving mother’s words: “I don’t want his death to be forgotten”
« J’avais un bon ado qui aimait les jeun: “I had a good teenager who loved young people,” Valérie, the late teen’s mother, tells us. She welcomes us into her home during this difficult time. An altar has been set up in the middle of the apartment in tribute to Jules.
Pour Valérie, perdre son fils unique est: For Valérie, losing her only son is the hardest ordeal she has ever had to go through. “He was my best friend,” she stresses. “He told me everything: his problems, his worries, his heartbreaks, etc. There were no secrets between us.” She had worked hard to build a special relationship with her son, and she never imagined she would have to say goodbye to him forever.
« C’était un bon garçon, organisé, ambit: “He was a good boy, organized, ambitious,” she says. “He was honest, never got into trouble. He had so much hope for his neighbourhood and for its young people! Basketball and young people were his whole life.” Deeply involved in his community, Jules was even planning to leave his part-time job at a café to devote himself full-time to community work.
« Il était tellement à son affaire et il: “He had it so together and he took good care of himself. He was active, he ate well, and he was a joy to live with,” she adds, devastated. Valérie still doesn’t understand why Jules had a heart attack and wonders whether her son had an undiagnosed health problem.
Très proche de sa mère, il était tout po: Very close to his mother, he was everything to her. “When he saw I was worried about him, he always reassured me by laughing with me or cracking jokes to make me laugh. When he came home late because of work, he always called to reassure me, to tell me where he was – when he got on the bus, when he arrived, down to the minute, etc.,” she recalls.
Si les moments qu’elle vit actuellement: While the moments she is living through now feel hazy and uncertain, she is convinced of one thing: her son’s death must not be ignored. “I don’t want his death to be forgotten, I want him to be remembered forever, for his kindness and his empathy.”
« J’ai un trou noir à la place du cœur »: “I have a black hole where my heart used to be,” Valérie says. “I lived for him. I hope he’ll be honoured for as long as possible,” she adds.
À gauche, Benjamin Dickson, agent pivot: Left, Benjamin Dickson, liaison officer for DOD Basketball. Right, Beverley Jacques, founder of the same organization and community worker.
Benjamin Dickson knew Jules well. Ben, as he’s known, is a coach at DOD Basketball. He met Jules when Jules was only 14. “Even when he was just a participant, at 14, he was the first to arrive and the last to leave. He was really motivated, he wanted to get involved a lot,” Benjamin recalls.
L’année suivante, une place d’animateur: The following year, a counsellor position opened up on the team. Jules didn’t hesitate to hand in his résumé. “He really wanted to get involved,” Benjamin Dickson repeats. “We gave him that opportunity, it was his first work experience, and from then on, he became a member of our family,” the 22-year-old coach tells us, looking pensive.
Alors que nous sommes assis dans un peti: As we sit in a small dog park, Beverley Jacques, founder of the organization DOD Basketball and community worker, joins us. He and Benjamin greet each other, joke around and sit down at a park table, while a few dogs come over to playfully beg us for pats.
« Jules était un ambassadeur. Il était t: “Jules was an ambassador. He was so motivated, he looked for solutions to everything and he had big plans,” Beverley begins. “When we made a deal with Starbucks for them to take on young people and hire them, he jumped at the chance right away,” he says.
Malgré cela, son amour pour sa communaut: Even so, his love for his community and his commitment to it, especially to the young people in his neighbourhood, were always on Jules’s mind. In a wave of nostalgia, Beverley takes out his phone to play us a message Jules left him a few days before his death, in which he can be heard saying: “I really want to go back to working full-time in the community sector, with the kids. I like Starbucks, but what I’m passionate about is basketball and you guys.”
« Lorsque la nouvelle de sa mort a comme: “When the news of his death started going around, everyone was shocked. Library staff, longtime friends and even former teachers came out last week to take part in the vigil held in his honour in the park where he lost his life,” added the community worker, who is in his forties. For him and Benjamin, the impact Jules had on his people is considerable.
« Et il a fait <em>tout</em> ça à 17 ans: “And he did all that at just 17,” Benjamin exclaims. “Inspiring young people, coaching others, raising their awareness, spreading joy around him, wanting to go further. He was already a role model for young people, when he was still one himself.”
Le terrain de basket où Jules a perdu la: The basketball court where Jules lost his life is located right behind the borough hall and the Saint-Léonard library.
« Dans un moment de tristesse comme ça,: “In a moment of sadness like this, we have to come a little closer together. We have to keep sticking together like the family we are,” Beverley says. He is also asking everyone who wishes to contribute to help young Jules’s parents, because they “have lost the only reason they had to keep working and living.”
L’association de DOD Basketball va entam: DOD Basketball will begin the process at the municipal level to have the court where Jules lost his life renamed after him. “That’s how we can do him justice, because his name and his story will go further than all of us, and that’s what he deserves,” Beverley believes. That’s the impact Jules had on him. “I’m frustrated that he’s not here anymore, but I laugh, I live, I watch his videos, I hear his voice, and I’ll keep carrying that spirit with me,” he adds.
Renommer un terrain en mémoire de Jules,: Renaming a court in Jules’s memory is also a way for the City of Montréal and the borough of Saint-Léonard to show young people that they listen to them, that they see them and that they consider them full-fledged citizens, the founder of DOD Basketball believes. “It’s also about giving Jules and everyone like him the respect they deserve. It’s a way of recognizing young people and their presence, of saying that we appreciate them and that we’re grateful for who they are,” he explains.
Le parc où se situe ledit terrain de bas: The park where the basketball court is located sits right in the heart of the borough of Saint-Léonard, just behind the borough hall. It borders the neighbourhood’s aquatic complex and library and is a few minutes’ walk from Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry high school, which the teenager attended.
Quelques jours après le drame, nous renc: A few days after the tragedy, late in the evening, we meet some young people shooting hoops on the court where Jules died. They tell us they would like the park renamed after him. “Jules was always here, and even if we didn’t know him personally, we all knew who he was,” explains Michael, one of the young people who play at the basketball court. “He was always training here. For sure, if they named this court after him, it would only make sense,” adds the 15-year-old, who is also passionate about basketball.
À Saint-Léonard, les membres du conseil: In Saint-Léonard, members of the borough council say they are “deeply affected by the death of young Jules Aurel Noukeu Jugnia.” Regarding the project to rename a place in the borough in his honour, the elected officials explain the following: “The city’s place-naming rules require meeting very specific criteria that apply to all boroughs” – which could lead to delays in renaming the court. For example, when a naming request is submitted in Montréal, the City of Montréal’s Comité de toponymie must review and approve the request before forwarding it to the borough concerned. In addition, one of the criteria the <l1>City requires be met when it comes to place names</l1> is that a place cannot bear the name of a person who died less than a year ago.
Le conseil assure toutefois ce qui suit: The council nevertheless gives the following assurance: “At the borough, we are reflecting on this and are in contact with local partners to find a way to honour his memory.”
Que faut-il faire à Montréal lorsqu’on v: What do you need to do in Montréal to rename a public place after someone’s death?
Il suffit de remplir un <l1>formulaire</: You simply fill out a detailed <l1>form</l1> describing what you want to do. The request is then reviewed by the City of Montréal’s Comité de toponymie, and then by the boroughs and public services concerned.
